A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLANSEARCH research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching reorganized material.

before.justification: v1 reports original code-generation evaluations on three benchmarks, alongside backtranslation, diversity, temperature, and base-versus-instruct experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds PLANSEARCH component ablations, o1-mini evaluations, and further public-filtering results.

M1.justification: The standard PLANSEARCH procedure remains unchanged. However, v2 Appendix K introduces an o1-specific adaptation that removes pseudocode generation, filters particular prompt words, and routes remaining refused queries to GPT-4o. These change the procedure for that model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate code generation on HumanEval+, MBPP+, and the May–September 2024 LiveCodeBench subset. Added models, ablations, and larger submission budgets do not introduce different datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Appendix K add the search-enabled o1-mini baseline, evaluated through direct and repeated sampling against its IDEASEARCH and PLANSEARCH variants. The earlier model comparisons and the Chain-of-Thought comparisons in Appendix E remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled experiments varying observation subset size, tree depth, and translation stages; one ablation doubles pipeline executions to match completion counts. The new o1-mini evaluation uses temperature and top-p of 1.0. Additional filtered comparisons display k through 1,000, although Appendix J's prose says 10,000. Existing benchmark protocols remain.

E4.justification: New Appendix H directly tests PLANSEARCH's subset size, observation depth, solution sketches, correction step, and pseudocode stage. Appendix K adds o1-mini diversity and refusal analysis, while Appendix J extends large-sample public-filtering comparisons. These substantially expand diagnostic evidence beyond v1's retained analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly specifies two complete pipeline executions for the no-fix/no-pseudocode ablation to equalize completion counts. This adds run-count information for a control, not uncertainty estimation. Confidence intervals and significance tests remain absent, and the pass@k estimator and dependence caveat are retained.

E6.justification: The original twelve Table 1 rows are unchanged. The newly reported o1-mini setting adds 69.5% pass@1 and pass@200 values of 90.8%, 91.2%, and 91.3% for repeated sampling, IDEASEARCH, and adapted PLANSEARCH. New ablation, diversity, and filtered curves add findings; Appendix K also reports unanswered queries falling from roughly 40% to below 0.5% after prompt filtering.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix M's finite diversity example is replaced by a general clique-counting derivation in v2 Appendix Q, including convergence to (k−1)/k and a balanced-versus-unbalanced frequency example (Equations 5–6). The underlying diversity definition and pass@k mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction remove the state-of-the-art characterization of the retained 77.0% result and qualify repeated-sampling comparisons as involving non-search models. The central contributions—planning to increase diversity and relating diversity to search gains—remain.

C2.justification: Appendix K newly attributes small o1-mini gains to search stacking and benchmark saturation, while Appendix H explains component and compute tradeoffs. Section 7 compresses the earlier warning about pass@k outside coding. The tree-search limitations are retained in Appendix R.

D1.justification: v2's abstract adds a code-repository access link absent from v1. Section 5.2 and Appendix K specify o1-mini API settings, filtered prompt words, and GPT-4o fallback behavior. Existing prompt templates are retained and relocated; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 expands positioning relative to program decomposition, training for reasoning, and tool-using agents, adding references including Parsel, STaR, Quiet-STaR, ReAct, and o1. The established search-and-planning framing remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, particularly in the abstract, diversity explanation, and limitations. It flattens the methods subsection hierarchy and reorders appendix material, including moving methodological future work to Appendix R. Most existing exposition is retained.

P2.justification: The appendix undergoes substantial visual restructuring: individual base/instruct plots become two nine-panel figures, and many retained plots are resized and packed together. Table 1 is reformatted, Figure 6 gains o1-mini points, and new experimental figures are added. New benchmark bar charts largely redisplay existing results.

improvement.justification: v2 adds direct component tests absent from v1 and usefully qualifies PLANSEARCH's benefits on o1-mini. Code-access information and the expanded diversity derivation also improve usefulness. The gains remain limited by the ablations' single model/benchmark setting and reporting inconsistencies, including the filtered-budget discrepancy and Appendix R's two-layer limitation despite the new L=3 experiment.
